* **Idle Undershoot Prevention**: * Restoring fuel at least 450 to 550 RPM above target idle gives combustion time to stabilize before reaching idle speed.
* **Highway Fuel Economy**: * Lowering `DFRPML` prolongs zero-fuel coast-down duration, saving fuel during gradual deceleration.
* **Hysteresis Protection**: * Governs fuel turn-on; paired with `DFRPMH` (fuel turn-off) to form the decel fuel cut operating envelope.

BATOFF.overview: BATOFF defines the fuel injector dead time latency offset curve indexed against electrical system battery voltage. Electromagnetic fuel injectors require a measurable time interval (dead time, typically 0.6 to 1.5 milliseconds) for the solenoid coil to build magnetic flux and pull the pintle off its seat before fuel begins spraying. As battery voltage decreases, solenoid opening velocity slows down significantly. BATOFF adds an offset pulsewidth that grows larger as system voltage sags, ensuring that effective fuel delivery remains constant regardless of alternator output or electrical accessories cycling on.
BATOFF.overview_markdown: `BATOFF` defines the fuel injector dead time latency offset curve indexed against electrical system battery voltage. Electromagnetic fuel injectors require a measurable time interval (dead time, typically 0.6 to 1.5 milliseconds) for the solenoid coil to build magnetic flux and pull the pintle off its seat before fuel begins spraying. As battery voltage decreases, solenoid opening velocity slows down significantly. `BATOFF` adds an offset pulsewidth that grows larger as system voltage sags, ensuring that effective fuel delivery remains constant regardless of alternator output or electrical accessories cycling on.
BATOFF.tuners_guide: BATOFF must be recalibrated whenever installing aftermarket fuel injectors, such as Bosch EV14 or Siemens Deka units. Modern high-impedance injectors have faster opening response and different voltage sensitivity curves compared to stock factory low-impedance or high-impedance pintle injectors. If BATOFF is miscalibrated, idle air-fuel ratio will swing lean or rich whenever heavy electrical loads engage, such as the radiator cooling fan, headlights, rear defroster, or air conditioning clutch. Raising BATOFF values increases dead time compensation, richening low-pulse operating conditions. Lowering BATOFF values decreases dead time compensation, preventing rich idle foul on fast modern injectors.
BATOFF.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Aftermarket Injector Characterization**: * Populate `BATOFF` with manufacturer-supplied voltage offset data when upgrading injectors to ensure stable air-fuel ratios.
* **Electrical Load Cycling Diagnosis**: * If idle air-fuel ratio dips rich or spikes lean when cooling fans cycle on, adjust `BATOFF` at the 12.0 to 13.5 Volt region.
* **Low-Pulsewidth Linearity**: * At idle and low load, dead time represents a large percentage of total pulsewidth; precise `BATOFF` calibration is vital for idle stability.
* **Failsafe Voltage Backup**: * If battery voltage reading is flagged faulty, the ECU automatically falls back to a 14.1 Volt default calibration index.
BATOFF.operating_conditions:
Takes effect continuously on every fuel injection pulse, adding battery voltage offset (dead time) to compensate for injector mechanical opening delays.

PRSHOT.overview: PRSHOT defines the single key-on injector priming pulsewidth delivered immediately upon turning the ignition key from off to run. Before the starter engages or the crankshaft begins rotating, the intake runners and intake valve backs may be completely dry. PRSHOT fires all fuel injectors simultaneously for a brief duration based on coolant temperature, pre-wetting the intake tracts with liquid fuel so that a combustible charge is available on the very first compression stroke. Colder coolant temperatures receive a larger priming charge, while hot restarts receive minimal or zero priming.
PRSHOT.overview_markdown: `PRSHOT` defines the single key-on injector priming pulsewidth delivered immediately upon turning the ignition key from off to run. Before the starter engages or the crankshaft begins rotating, the intake runners and intake valve backs may be completely dry. `PRSHOT` fires all fuel injectors simultaneously for a brief duration based on coolant temperature, pre-wetting the intake tracts with liquid fuel so that a combustible charge is available on the very first compression stroke. Colder coolant temperatures receive a larger priming charge, while hot restarts receive minimal or zero priming.
PRSHOT.tuners_guide: PRSHOT is critical for fast, crisp starting response. On cold mornings, an adequate prime shot allows the engine to catch on the first or second starter revolution. However, when upgrading to high-flow fuel injectors, PRSHOT must be scaled downward by the injector size ratio. If large injectors are installed and PRSHOT is left at stock values, the single prime shot will spray too much raw liquid fuel into the cylinders, fouling spark plugs before the starter turns. Zeroing out PRSHOT is common on race applications or vehicles running auxiliary starting fuels to prevent flooding.

RNFPRD.overview: RNFPRD defines the fuel injection start-to-run transfer distributor pulse period threshold. During starter cranking, the engine controller delivers rich, fixed-duration cranking priming pulses to wet the intake manifold runners and spark ignition. Once the engine catches and spins past RNFPRD, the controller cuts off cranking enrichment pulses and initiates normal running speed-density fuel calculation. In period-based logic, smaller count values represent faster engine speeds. In factory calibrations, RNFPRD is set to 48 counts, corresponding to approximately 625 RPM. Grouped under the Start-to-Run Transfer category in calibration templates, RNFPRD synchronizes the fueling transition with the ignition transition.
RNFPRD.overview_markdown: `RNFPRD` defines the fuel injection start-to-run transfer distributor pulse period threshold. During starter cranking, the engine controller delivers rich, fixed-duration cranking priming pulses to wet the intake manifold runners and spark ignition. Once the engine catches and spins past `RNFPRD`, the controller cuts off cranking enrichment pulses and initiates normal running speed-density fuel calculation. In period-based logic, smaller count values represent faster engine speeds. In factory calibrations, `RNFPRD` is set to 48 counts, corresponding to approximately 625 RPM. Grouped under the Start-to-Run Transfer category in calibration templates, `RNFPRD` synchronizes the fueling transition with the ignition transition.
RNFPRD.tuners_guide: In period units, raising RNFPRD transitions to running speed-density fueling at a lower engine speed (e.g., 60 counts ≈ 500 RPM). This is advantageous when installing oversized aftermarket fuel injectors (such as +40% or 52+ lb/hr units), where prolonged cranking pulses quickly flood the cylinders and foul spark plugs on warm restarts. Lowering RNFPRD extends cranking enrichment to a higher engine speed (e.g., 38 counts ≈ 789 RPM), which helps cold starts catch solidly by maintaining rich priming fuel until the engine flares fully.
RNFPRD.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Preventing Large Injector Flooding**: * When running large aftermarket injectors, raising `RNFPRD` cuts off rich cranking priming pulses earlier, preventing cylinder flooding on hot restarts.
* **Cold Start Flare Support**: * On alcohol or E85 conversions, lowering `RNFPRD` keeps rich cranking fuel active higher into the start flare to prevent cold die-out.
* **Period Scaling**: * Period is inversely related to RPM: RPM ≈ 30,000 / count. Factory setting 48 counts = 625 RPM.

STFPRD.overview: STFPRD defines the fuel injection run-to-start stall hysteresis distributor pulse period threshold. Once the engine is running on normal speed-density fuel calculations, if engine speed sags severely (such as during abrupt clutch release, severe load, or an impending stall), speed-density manifold pressure readings become erratic and fuel injectors cannot deliver stable small pulsewidths. If the distributor pulse period exceeds STFPRD (engine speed falls below approximately 460 RPM in factory calibrations), the engine controller recognizes an impending stall, drops running fuel mode, and re-engages starting/cranking fuel enrichment logic to catch the falling engine and prevent stalling.
STFPRD.overview_markdown: `STFPRD` defines the fuel injection run-to-start stall hysteresis distributor pulse period threshold. Once the engine is running on normal speed-density fuel calculations, if engine speed sags severely (such as during abrupt clutch release, severe load, or an impending stall), speed-density manifold pressure readings become erratic and fuel injectors cannot deliver stable small pulsewidths. If the distributor pulse period exceeds `STFPRD` (engine speed falls below approximately 460 RPM in factory calibrations), the engine controller recognizes an impending stall, drops running fuel mode, and re-engages starting/cranking fuel enrichment logic to catch the falling engine and prevent stalling.
STFPRD.tuners_guide: In period units, raising STFPRD allows the engine to drop to a lower engine speed (e.g., 80 counts ≈ 375 RPM) before re-engaging cranking fuel. This prevents sudden rich fuel dumping when lugging the engine at very low speeds in manual transmission cars. Lowering STFPRD re-engages cranking fuel at a higher engine speed (e.g., 55 counts ≈ 545 RPM), dropping back to cranking enrichment sooner to assist stall recovery, but setting it too close to target idle speed can cause idle dips to flood the engine.
STFPRD.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Fuel Stall Recovery Deadband**: * Factory setting of 460 RPM (65 counts) sits 165 RPM below the start-to-run transfer threshold (`RNFPRD` at 625 RPM), preventing mode-switching hunting.
* **Anti-Lug Tuning for Manual Transmissions**: * Raising `STFPRD` prevents sudden rich bogging when heavily loading the engine at low speeds in parking lots or stop-and-go traffic.
* **Period Scaling Reminder**: * Period counts are inversely proportional to RPM (RPM ≈ 30000 / count).

STRTFL.overview: STRTFL defines the base cranking fuel delivery curve indexed against engine coolant temperature during starter cranking. When starting a cold engine, fuel droplets condense onto cold intake runners, intake valves, and cylinder walls rather than remaining suspended in the intake airflow. To establish an ignitable air-fuel vapor cloud in the combustion chamber, STRTFL provides heavy initial fuel pulsewidths at low coolant temperatures, tapering down smoothly as the engine warms toward operating temperature. The engine controller uses this base table while the starter motor is actively rotating the crankshaft below running speed.
STRTFL.overview_markdown: `STRTFL` defines the base cranking fuel delivery curve indexed against engine coolant temperature during starter cranking. When starting a cold engine, fuel droplets condense onto cold intake runners, intake valves, and cylinder walls rather than remaining suspended in the intake airflow. To establish an ignitable air-fuel vapor cloud in the combustion chamber, `STRTFL` provides heavy initial fuel pulsewidths at low coolant temperatures, tapering down smoothly as the engine warms toward operating temperature. The engine controller uses this base table while the starter motor is actively rotating the crankshaft below running speed.
STRTFL.tuners_guide: Tuning STRTFL is required when installing larger fuel injectors or converting to alternative fuels like E85. When upgrading to higher-flow injectors, scale the entire STRTFL curve downward by the injector flow ratio to prevent rich spark plug fouling and hard hot-restarts. When calibrating for E85, cold cranking fuel must be increased by 30 to 45 percent at low coolant temperatures because ethanol has a high latent heat of vaporization. Raising table values assists cold starting in winter weather when the engine coughs but fails to catch. Lowering table values eliminates fuel odor, black exhaust smoke, and flooded engine conditions during warm cranking.
STRTFL.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Injector Size Scaling**: * When installing larger injectors, scale the entire `STRTFL` table downward by the flow ratio (stock flow divided by new flow) to avoid flooding.
* **E85 and Cold Weather Tuning**: * Increase values by 30 to 45 percent at low temperatures when running E85 or in sub-freezing climates to ensure reliable ignition.
* **Warm Start Behavior**: * Lowering values eliminates black exhaust smoke and flooded spark plugs on hot restarts.
* **Starting Symptoms**: * If the engine spins without catching on cold mornings, raise the lower temperature points incrementally.

STRLMT.overview: STRLMT defines the minimum coolant temperature floor permitted for cranking fuel calculations when starting at closed throttle. Because the STRTFL starting fuel calculation squares the table lookup result, unconstrained sub-zero temperature sensor readings could command excessive injector pulsewidths that flood the cylinders. In factory calibrations, STRLMT is set to 105 counts, corresponding to approximately 38 degF. If an engine is cranked with the throttle closed at temperatures colder than 38 degF, the controller clamps the input temperature to 38 degF, preventing excessive cranking fuel accumulation.
STRLMT.overview_markdown: `STRLMT` defines the minimum coolant temperature floor permitted for cranking fuel calculations when starting at closed throttle. Because the `STRTFL` starting fuel calculation squares the table lookup result, unconstrained sub-zero temperature sensor readings could command excessive injector pulsewidths that flood the cylinders. In factory calibrations, `STRLMT` is set to 105 counts, corresponding to approximately 38 degF. If an engine is cranked with the throttle closed at temperatures colder than 38 degF, the controller clamps the input temperature to 38 degF, preventing excessive cranking fuel accumulation.
STRLMT.tuners_guide: Raising STRLMT limits cold starting fuel delivery during freezing weather, which helps prevent flooded spark plugs when running high-flow aftermarket fuel injectors. Lowering STRLMT allows the cranking fuel routine to follow STRTFL down to lower sub-freezing temperatures, providing additional fuel for harsh winter conditions on pump gas or ethanol fuels. Setting STRLMT higher than normal operating temperature locks the cranking routine into warm start fueling regardless of ambient temperature. If cold starting at closed throttle is stubborn, lowering STRLMT provides more fuel, while opening the throttle off-idle bypasses STRLMT entirely.
STRLMT.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Cold Cranking Protection**: * Raising `STRLMT` caps the maximum cranking pulsewidth, preventing wet-fouling on large injectors in freezing weather.
* **Sub-Zero & E85 Cold Starts**: * Lowering `STRLMT` allows richer fueling below 38 degF for cold northern climates or E85 conversions.
* **Closed-Throttle Gating**: * `STRLMT` is only applied when the throttle is fully closed; cracking the throttle off-idle bypasses the clamp immediately.
* **Stock Calibration Matching**: * Factory setting of 105 counts (38 degF) balances cold fuel vaporization against the risk of unburned fuel flooding.
STRLMT.operating_conditions:
Takes effect if an engine is cranked with the throttle closed at temperatures colder than 38 degF, the controller clamps the input temperature to 38 degF, preventing excessive cranking fuel accumulation.

STFTMP.overview: STFTMP defines a temperature-dependent reduction factor that subtracts fuel from the cranking calculation as the engine warms up. While STRTFL sets the cold base starting fuel, warm and hot engines require significantly less fuel to start because hot metal surfaces promote immediate fuel vaporization. Working in direct multiplication with the barometric reduction factor (STFBAR), STFTMP calculates a combined reduction percentage. This percentage subtracts fuel from the cranking pulsewidth, ensuring hot restarts are clean and rapid without flooding or black smoke.
STFTMP.overview_markdown: `STFTMP` defines a temperature-dependent reduction factor that subtracts fuel from the cranking calculation as the engine warms up. While `STRTFL` sets the cold base starting fuel, warm and hot engines require significantly less fuel to start because hot metal surfaces promote immediate fuel vaporization. Working in direct multiplication with the barometric reduction factor (`STFBAR`), `STFTMP` calculates a combined reduction percentage. This percentage subtracts fuel from the cranking pulsewidth, ensuring hot restarts are clean and rapid without flooding or black smoke.
STFTMP.tuners_guide: Tuning STFTMP resolves hard warm-starting issues, extended hot cranking, and fuel odor upon restart. If an engine restarts with difficulty when warm, exhibiting a heavy gasoline smell or requiring partial throttle to catch, increase STFTMP at warm coolant temperatures. This increases the reduction factor, taking more fuel out of the cranking calculation. Conversely, if a warm engine fires and immediately dies or pops back through the intake manifold, reduce STFTMP values to preserve more cranking fuel. For ethanol blends, hot restart fuel should be preserved to combat fuel vaporization in the rail.
STFTMP.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Warm Restart Flooding**: * Increasing `STFTMP` values at warm temperatures (above 140 degF) removes excess cranking fuel, curing hot restart flooding.
* **Lean Hot-Start Pop**: * Lowering `STFTMP` values retains more cranking pulsewidth if warm restarts pop lean or crank excessively before catching.
* **Altitude Compounding**: * Because `STFTMP` is multiplied by `STFBAR`, changes here interact directly with high-elevation starting behavior.
* **Injector Upgrades**: * When running large aftermarket injectors, higher `STFTMP` reduction factors prevent rich hot-cranking stumbles.
STFTMP.operating_conditions:

EPPMUL.overview: EPPMUL defines a multiplicative fuel decay factor indexed against crankshaft revolutions during engine starting. When the starter motor begins cranking, maximum fuel pulsewidth is required on the initial rotations to wet dry intake runners and establish a combustible vapor cloud. If the engine does not start immediately, continuous delivery of maximum starting fuel would quickly wet-foul spark plugs. EPPMUL scales down the cranking pulsewidth with each engine position pulse, reducing fueling smoothly over extended cranking sessions to preserve battery life and prevent cylinder wash.
EPPMUL.overview_markdown: `EPPMUL` defines a multiplicative fuel decay factor indexed against crankshaft revolutions during engine starting. When the starter motor begins cranking, maximum fuel pulsewidth is required on the initial rotations to wet dry intake runners and establish a combustible vapor cloud. If the engine does not start immediately, continuous delivery of maximum starting fuel would quickly wet-foul spark plugs. `EPPMUL` scales down the cranking pulsewidth with each engine position pulse, reducing fueling smoothly over extended cranking sessions to preserve battery life and prevent cylinder wash.
EPPMUL.tuners_guide: Adjusting EPPMUL improves extended cranking reliability and cures warm-start flooding. If an engine fires immediately on the first revolution but dies if it fails to catch instantly, raise the tail of EPPMUL to maintain adequate fuel delivery during extended cranking. For engines equipped with high-flow aftermarket fuel injectors that flood easily, lower the curve so starting fuel decays more steeply after the first four to six crankshaft revolutions. Raising the initial table points aids very cold morning starting where additional revolutions are needed before combustion catches.
EPPMUL.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Extended Cranking Tuning**: * If the engine fires initially but dies during prolonged cranking, raise the higher-revolution points of `EPPMUL`.
* **Aftermarket Injector Flooding**: * High-flow injectors flood cold cylinders quickly; steepen the decay curve so fuel tapers down rapidly after the first 4 to 6 rotations.
* **Cold Weather Reliability**: * Increasing values across the middle of the curve maintains sufficient fuel vapor during sluggish starter rotation in winter.
* **E85 Adaptations**: * E85 requires a slower decay rate because ethanol requires more revolutions to generate sufficient vapor heat.
EPPMUL.operating_conditions:

STFBAR.overview: STFBAR defines the barometric pressure compensation curve for cranking fuel delivery. At high altitudes or during low ambient barometric pressure conditions, the air is less dense and contains fewer oxygen molecules per cylinder fill. If sea-level cranking fuel were injected at mountain elevations, the air-fuel mixture would be excessively rich, causing spark plug fouling and extended cranking. STFBAR generates an altitude-based reduction factor that scales down cranking fuel as atmospheric pressure decreases.
STFBAR.overview_markdown: `STFBAR` defines the barometric pressure compensation curve for cranking fuel delivery. At high altitudes or during low ambient barometric pressure conditions, the air is less dense and contains fewer oxygen molecules per cylinder fill. If sea-level cranking fuel were injected at mountain elevations, the air-fuel mixture would be excessively rich, causing spark plug fouling and extended cranking. `STFBAR` generates an altitude-based reduction factor that scales down cranking fuel as atmospheric pressure decreases.
STFBAR.tuners_guide: STFBAR ensures crisp starting when operating vehicles at high elevations, such as mountain regions or high-altitude race tracks. If a vehicle starts cleanly at sea level but floods or cranks sluggishly with black exhaust smoke in the mountains, increase STFBAR values at lower barometric pressures. If high-altitude cold starting is excessively lean or backfires in the intake, lower STFBAR values to preserve more base cranking fuel. When converting to a 3-bar MAP sensor, verify that barometric pressure readings at key-on properly align with STFBAR scaling.
STFBAR.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **High Altitude Starting**: * Increasing `STFBAR` values removes cranking fuel at low barometric pressures, preventing flooded plugs in mountain passes.
* **Sea Level Preservation**: * Keep `STFBAR` at zero near sea-level pressure (14.7 psi absolute) so full cold start enrichment is delivered.
* **3-Bar MAP Sensor Calibration**: * Barometric pressure is sampled from the MAP sensor at key-on; ensure sensor transfer curves match the sensor hardware.
* **Lean Stumble at Altitude**: * If high-altitude starts pop lean, decrease `STFBAR` reduction factors to restore cranking pulsewidth.
STFBAR.operating_conditions:

SFDCAY.overview: SFDCAY defines the initial fuel enrichment pulsewidth loaded at the instant the engine catches and transfers from cranking into running mode. When the engine first fires and engine speed exceeds the cranking threshold, intake manifold airflow undergoes a sudden surge while manifold vacuum is not yet stable. SFDCAY provides a rich fuel bridge that decays smoothly into the steady-state running fuel tables, cushioning the abrupt physical transition and preventing lean hesitation, idle sag, or stall. The initial decay value is looked up based on engine coolant temperature.
SFDCAY.overview_markdown: `SFDCAY` defines the initial fuel enrichment pulsewidth loaded at the instant the engine catches and transfers from cranking into running mode. When the engine first fires and engine speed exceeds the cranking threshold, intake manifold airflow undergoes a sudden surge while manifold vacuum is not yet stable. `SFDCAY` provides a rich fuel bridge that decays smoothly into the steady-state running fuel tables, cushioning the abrupt physical transition and preventing lean hesitation, idle sag, or stall. The initial decay value is looked up based on engine coolant temperature.
SFDCAY.tuners_guide: SFDCAY is the primary calibration parameter for curing start-and-stall behavior, where an engine starts instantly on the key but stalls the moment the starter is released. Raising SFDCAY provides a richer, more resilient fuel bridge that stabilizes idle speed on cold mornings or when running aggressive aftermarket camshafts with low idle vacuum. Lowering SFDCAY prevents overly rich stumbling, black exhaust smoke, and fouled plugs when restarting a warm engine. When calibrating for larger fuel injectors, scale SFDCAY downward proportionally with the injector flow rate.
SFDCAY.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Curing Start-and-Stall**: * If an engine starts readily but immediately stumbles or dies when the key returns to the run position, increase `SFDCAY` at that coolant temperature.
* **Aftermarket Camshafts**: * Performance camshafts have poor low-speed vacuum and sluggish air velocity; raise `SFDCAY` to provide extra fuel cushioning until idle stabilizes.
* **Injector Scaling**: * Scale `SFDCAY` downward when installing higher-flow injectors to prevent rich loading upon start-to-run transition.
* **Warm Restart Drivability**: * Lowering values above 140 degF cleans up exhaust smell and stabilizes hot idle flare.
SFDCAY.operating_conditions:

MAPOFS.overview: MAPOFS_BoostMapOffsetForDCWOT establishes the manifold pressure threshold below target boost where wastegate solenoid closed-loop modulation begins. While manifold pressure is far below the boost target (e.g. during initial spool-up), the wastegate should remain clamped 100% shut to achieve the fastest possible spool. Once manifold pressure climbs within MAPOFS of target boost, the ECU transitions into modulating wastegate duty cycle to prevent overshooting.

RPMMAP.overview: RPMMAP defines the manifold pressure threshold curve across engine speed that separates the increasing part-throttle enrichment zone from the decreasing part-throttle enrichment zone. During moderate to heavy acceleration before wide-open throttle is reached, the engine controller requires open-loop fuel enrichment to prevent lean misfires and assist turbocharger spool-up. The controller looks up the switchpoint from RPMMAP based on current engine speed and compares it to manifold absolute pressure. When manifold pressure exceeds the curve, the controller increments the open-loop enrichment multiplier. When manifold pressure falls below the curve, the controller decrements the enrichment multiplier back toward baseline. The factory curve transitions from positive boost of approximately 3.1 psi at 2900 RPM down to 9.2 psi of vacuum at 5200 RPM.
RPMMAP.overview_markdown: `RPMMAP` defines the manifold pressure threshold curve across engine speed that separates the increasing part-throttle enrichment zone from the decreasing part-throttle enrichment zone. During moderate to heavy acceleration before wide-open throttle is reached, the engine controller requires open-loop fuel enrichment to prevent lean misfires and assist turbocharger spool-up. The controller looks up the switchpoint from `RPMMAP` based on current engine speed and compares it to manifold absolute pressure. When manifold pressure exceeds the curve, the controller increments the open-loop enrichment multiplier. When manifold pressure falls below the curve, the controller decrements the enrichment multiplier back toward baseline. The factory curve transitions from positive boost of approximately 3.1 psi at 2900 RPM down to 9.2 psi of vacuum at 5200 RPM.
RPMMAP.tuners_guide: Adjust RPMMAP to control the engine load threshold where aggressive part-throttle boost enrichment begins. Lowering table pressure values causes the controller to trigger part-throttle enrichment earlier in the manifold pressure sweep, eliminating lean flat spots and hesitation during moderate pedal tip-in. Raising table pressure values delays enrichment until higher manifold boost levels are attained, improving fuel economy during light-load highway cruising. RPMMAP.tuners_guide_markdown:

PTENR.overview: PTENR establishes the engine position pulse countdown interval and step size governing how rapidly part-throttle enrichment ramps upward when manifold pressure exceeds the RPMMAP boundary curve. Formatted as a 16-bit word, the high byte defines the number of distributor reference pulses that must elapse between enrichment steps, while the low byte defines the increment added to the open-loop enrichment fraction timer. This pulse countdown structure ensures that transient enrichment builds progressively with engine revolutions rather than jumping instantaneously, providing a smooth transition into boost. The factory setting of 50 pulses and 1 count increment ensures that enrichment builds smoothly over approximately 25 engine revolutions on a four-cylinder engine.

The factory setting of 50 pulses and 1 count increment ensures that enrichment builds smoothly over approximately 25 engine revolutions on a four-cylinder engine.
PTENR.tuners_guide: Calibrate PTENR to tune the ramp-in rate of part-throttle boost enrichment. Lowering the pulse countdown value in the high byte causes the enrichment multiplier to ramp upward faster, curing hesitation, lean air-fuel ratio spikes, or sluggish turbocharger spool-up when rolling into the throttle. Raising the pulse countdown value slows down the rate of enrichment buildup, creating a more conservative ramp that conserves fuel during brief transient accelerations. Increasing the low byte step value increases the percentage added on each countdown expiration, producing a more aggressive step-up.
PTENR.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Faster Enrichment Ramp**: Lowering the pulse countdown value in the high byte causes the enrichment multiplier to ramp upward faster, curing hesitation, lean air-fuel ratio spikes, or sluggish turbocharger spool-up when rolling into the throttle.
* **Gentler Ramp and Fuel Economy**: Raising the pulse countdown value slows down the rate of enrichment buildup, creating a more conservative ramp that conserves fuel during brief transient accelerations.
* **Step Size Adjustment**: Increasing the low byte step value increases the percentage added on each countdown expiration, producing a more aggressive step-up.
* **Injector Upgrades**: When running very large injectors, ensure the ramp-in rate is not overly rapid to prevent transient rich bogging.
PTENR.operating_conditions:
Takes effect when manifold pressure exceeds the RPMMAP boundary curve.

PTENR2.overview: PTENR2 sets the distributor reference pulse countdown interval governing the decay rate of part-throttle enrichment when manifold pressure falls below the RPMMAP boundary curve. When the driver modulates or lifts off the throttle after accelerating in boost, the engine controller must taper off transient enrichment smoothly to prevent sudden lean surges or unnecessary fuel waste. PTENR2 defines how many engine position pulses must occur before the controller decrements the open-loop fraction timer by the negative step value in PTENRD. PTENR2.tuners_guide: Adjust PTENR2 to optimize how quickly transient enrichment decays when exiting boost. Lowering the pulse countdown value causes part-throttle enrichment to decay away more rapidly, returning the engine to standard closed-loop or baseline fueling faster to improve fuel economy. Raising the pulse countdown value sustains enrichment longer after lifting off the throttle, which helps prevent lean popping in the exhaust during rapid gear shifts or when feathering the throttle in road-course driving. * **Coordination with PTENRD**: Coordinate changes to `PTENR2` with the step decrement value in `PTENRD` to control total decay curve slope.
* **Drivability Tuning**: Set high enough to prevent lean bucking when rolling off the throttle at highway speeds.

PTENRD.overview: PTENRD specifies the signed step decrement added to the open-loop fraction timer on each decay interval when manifold pressure falls below the RPMMAP boundary curve. Stored as an 8-bit two's complement negative integer, the factory setting of 255 counts represents minus one count, subtracting one fractional increment from the enrichment multiplier every PTENR2 pulse interval. Furthermore, PTENRD is used in the hysteresis math that clears the maximum part-throttle enrichment status flag, ensuring that spark timing returns smoothly to normal advance schedules after boost enrichment ends.

PTENRD.tuners_guide: Configure PTENRD to control the step size of transient fuel decay when exiting boost. Because PTENRD is also multiplied by PTENUM in the spark advance hysteresis check, changing this value alters the decay window required to clear the maximum enrichment spark status flag.

PTENUM.overview: PTENUM defines the hysteresis threshold multiplier required to clear the part-throttle enrichment maximum flag and return ignition advance to standard running schedules after transient enrichment has peaked. When part-throttle enrichment reaches the upper ceiling defined by PTELMT and PTEADJ, the engine controller asserts a status flag that substitutes specialized spark advance curves. Once engine load subsides and transient enrichment decays, the multiplier must drop below the ceiling by a specific margin before the controller clears the flag and restores normal ignition timing. PTENUM establishes this margin by multiplying the negated decrement value from PTENRD. The factory setting of 15 counts requires a drop of 15 counts before normal spark advance resumes.

When part-throttle enrichment reaches the upper ceiling defined by `PTELMT` and `PTEADJ`, the engine controller asserts a status flag that substitutes specialized spark advance curves. Once engine load subsides and transient enrichment decays, the multiplier must drop below the ceiling by a specific margin before the controller clears the flag and restores normal ignition timing. `PTENUM` establishes this margin by multiplying the negated decrement value from `PTENRD`. The factory setting of 15 counts requires a drop of 15 counts before normal spark advance resumes.
PTENUM.tuners_guide: Tune PTENUM to stabilize ignition timing transitions following hard part-throttle acceleration. Increasing PTENUM broadens the hysteresis window, keeping modified ignition timing active longer after peak enrichment is reached. This prevents rapid chattering between standard spark advance and enrichment spark advance when modulating the throttle near the ceiling threshold. Decreasing PTENUM narrows the hysteresis window, allowing the controller to restore baseline spark advance sooner as soon as the throttle is relaxed. Avoid setting PTENUM to zero, which can cause erratic spark oscillation near the limit.
PTENUM.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Spark Hysteresis Window**: Increasing `PTENUM` broadens the hysteresis window, keeping modified ignition timing active longer after peak enrichment is reached.
* **Preventing Timing Chattering**: Prevents rapid chattering between standard spark advance and enrichment spark advance when modulating the throttle near the ceiling threshold.
* **Restoring Base Timing Sooner**: Decreasing `PTENUM` narrows the hysteresis window, allowing the controller to restore baseline spark advance sooner as soon as the throttle is relaxed.
* **Zero Setting Warning**: Avoid setting `PTENUM` to zero, which can cause erratic spark oscillation near the limit.

PTEADJ.overview: PTEADJ provides signed manifold pressure-dependent scaling to the part-throttle enrichment ceiling established by PTELMT. Because engine air density and knock vulnerability vary dramatically across vacuum and positive boost, a static RPM ceiling is insufficient. PTEADJ modifies the maximum allowable enrichment multiplier based on instantaneous manifold absolute pressure. In calibration software, zero counts represents a neutral 1.00 multiplier, leaving the RPM ceiling unchanged. Negative and positive values in PTEADJ scale the enrichment ceiling down or up, providing extra fuel headroom at high boost while capping enrichment at light loads.

Increasing table values in the positive boost region raises the maximum enrichment ceiling, ensuring that heavily boosted engines receive sufficient fuel under sustained part-throttle acceleration. Lowering values in moderate vacuum or low boost ranges prevents excessive fuel buildup during mild acceleration. When converting to a 3-bar MAP sensor, verify that table pressure axis breakpoints are updated so that boost-dependent ceiling scaling takes effect at the intended real-world manifold pressures.

* **Signed Table Behavior**: Remember that zero represents a neutral 1.00 multiplier in firmware math. Positive and negative offsets scale the RPM limit proportionally.
* **3-Bar MAP Alignment**: When converting to a 3-bar MAP sensor, verify that table pressure axis breakpoints are updated so that boost-dependent ceiling scaling takes effect at the intended real-world manifold pressures.

BAROCP.overview: BAROCP defines the barometric pressure compensation curve for warm-up fuel enrichment. At higher elevations with reduced atmospheric pressure and thinner air, the engine requires less supplementary fuel during warm-up because air mass per cylinder stroke is naturally lower. BAROCP scales down the total accumulated warm-up enrichment factor as barometric pressure decreases. This table prevents rich stumbling, carbon foul on spark plugs, and excessive exhaust emissions during cold engine warm-up in high-altitude environments.
BAROCP.overview_markdown: `BAROCP` defines the barometric pressure compensation curve for warm-up fuel enrichment. At higher elevations with reduced atmospheric pressure and thinner air, the engine requires less supplementary fuel during warm-up because air mass per cylinder stroke is naturally lower. `BAROCP` scales down the total accumulated warm-up enrichment factor as barometric pressure decreases. This table prevents rich stumbling, carbon foul on spark plugs, and excessive exhaust emissions during cold engine warm-up in high-altitude environments.
BAROCP.tuners_guide: BAROCP ensures consistent cold drivability when driving across varying elevations. In factory calibrations, BAROCP maintains 100% warm-up fueling at sea level (14.7 psi absolute) and tapers fuel slightly at mountain elevations. If operating a vehicle primarily at high altitudes (such as Denver or mountain passes above 5,000 feet) and the engine experiences rich hesitation or dark exhaust smoke during warm-up, increase the barometric reduction in BAROCP. If cold warm-up operation at high elevations is lean, flatten the curve toward zero reduction to preserve full warm-up fueling.
BAROCP.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **High Altitude Warm-Up Tuning**: * If cold driveaway in the mountains produces black smoke and rich stumbling, increase the reduction factor at low barometric pressures.
* **Sea Level Retention**: * Keep `BAROCP` at zero reduction near 14.7 psi barometric pressure so sea-level warm-up enrichment remains unaffected.
* **3-Bar MAP Sensor Calibration**: * Barometric pressure is sampled from the MAP sensor at key-on; verify sensor transfer curves match the sensor hardware.
* **Multiplicative Scale**: * Multiplies the entire accumulated cold enrichment sum (`Temp0`) before charge temperature compensation.

Takes effect during cold starts and warm-up driving at altitude, adjusting warm-up fuel enrichment based on ambient barometric pressure.

AIRTMP.overview: AIRTMP defines the intake air charge temperature fuel compensation curve. Ambient and compressed air density varies inversely with temperature: cold air is dense and contains more oxygen molecules per volume, while hot compressed charge air is less dense. AIRTMP reads the raw intake charge temperature sensor voltage (where higher voltage represents colder air and lower voltage represents hot compressed air) and scales fuel pulsewidth accordingly. This table provides weather compensation across freezing winter and blistering summer conditions, as well as compensating for turbocharger intercooler heat soak.

Ambient and compressed air density varies inversely with temperature: cold air is dense and contains more oxygen molecules per volume, while hot compressed charge air is less dense. `AIRTMP` reads the raw intake charge temperature sensor voltage (where higher voltage represents colder air and lower voltage represents hot compressed air) and scales fuel pulsewidth accordingly. This table provides weather compensation across freezing winter and blistering summer conditions, as well as compensating for turbocharger intercooler heat soak.
AIRTMP.tuners_guide: AIRTMP ensures consistent air-fuel ratios across varying weather conditions and intercooler temperatures. In sub-freezing winter driving, AIRTMP adds enrichment (up to +25 percent fuel) to prevent lean combustion under dense ambient air. On hot summer track days or after repeated high-boost pulls where intercooler heat soak causes charge air temperatures to spike, AIRTMP tapers fuel delivery to prevent overly rich, sluggish operation. Remember that sensor voltage is inverted relative to temperature: high voltage represents cold air, and low voltage represents hot air. If cold-weather acceleration runs lean, raise values at the high-voltage end of the curve.
AIRTMP.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Cold Weather Density Compensation**: * Increases fueling in freezing ambient conditions to prevent lean combustion from dense winter air.
* **Intercooler Heat Soak Trimming**: * Reduces pulsewidth under hot charge air conditions (low sensor voltage), preventing rich bogging on consecutive boost pulls.
* **Inverted Voltage Axis**: * Sensor voltage is inversely proportional to temperature: high voltage (4.0 to 5.0 Volts) = cold air; low voltage (0.0 to 1.5 Volts) = hot air.
* **Lineage from T2 Calibration**: * Copied from the factory 1989 T2 calibration into T-SBECII to support charge temperature sensor equipped engines.

Takes effect continuously across all running conditions, adjusting fuel delivery based on intake air charge temperature to compensate for air density changes.

POSTRG.overview: POSTRG defines the minimum rate of throttle position sensor voltage increase required to trigger a throttle-based acceleration enrichment pump shot. When the driver presses the accelerator pedal, the throttle blade opens before the intake manifold plenum can fill with air and register an increased pressure reading. To prevent an immediate lean hesitation or stumble, the engine controller calculates the difference between instantaneous throttle voltage and a rolling average throttle voltage. If this delta exceeds POSTRG, the controller activates acceleration pump fueling. The factory setting of 3 counts represents approximately 0.06 volts, filtering out minor driver foot vibrations, electrical noise, and road bumps while ensuring immediate response to deliberate pedal inputs.
POSTRG.overview_markdown: `POSTRG` defines the minimum rate of throttle position sensor voltage increase required to trigger a throttle-based acceleration enrichment pump shot. When the driver presses the accelerator pedal, the throttle blade opens before the intake manifold plenum can fill with air and register an increased pressure reading. To prevent an immediate lean hesitation or stumble, the engine controller calculates the difference between instantaneous throttle voltage and a rolling average throttle voltage. If this delta exceeds `POSTRG`, the controller activates acceleration pump fueling. The factory setting of 3 counts represents approximately 0.06 volts, filtering out minor driver foot vibrations, electrical noise, and road bumps while ensuring immediate response to deliberate pedal inputs.
POSTRG.tuners_guide: Lowering POSTRG makes the throttle acceleration pump more sensitive, firing extra fuel on very small throttle inputs to eliminate hairline tip-in hesitations. However, setting this value to zero or near zero can cause false pump shots from throttle shaft vibration or road roughness, degrading fuel economy and causing subtle rich surges during highway cruising. Raising POSTRG requires a firmer pedal depression before enrichment activates, which may be beneficial with oversized aftermarket throttle bodies where small angular openings flow significantly more air.
POSTRG.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Tip-in Sensitivity**: Lowering `POSTRG` makes the throttle acceleration pump more sensitive, firing extra fuel on very small throttle inputs to eliminate hairline tip-in hesitations.
* **Preventing False Triggers**: Setting this value to zero or near zero can cause false pump shots from throttle shaft vibration or road roughness, degrading fuel economy and causing subtle rich surges during highway cruising.
* **Large Throttle Bodies**: Raising `POSTRG` requires a firmer pedal depression before enrichment activates, which may be beneficial with oversized aftermarket throttle bodies where small angular openings flow significantly more air.
* **Coordination with POSSLP**: Always adjust `POSTRG` in coordination with the gain slope in `POSSLP`.

THRMAX.overview: THRMAX defines the maximum allowable throttle position sensor delta voltage used to compute the throttle-based acceleration enrichment pump shot. When the accelerator is rapidly floored from idle, the throttle sensor voltage can jump by more than 3.5 volts in a fraction of a second. If this entire voltage swing were multiplied by the enrichment slope, the controller would inject a massive flood of fuel that would bog or drown the engine. THRMAX clamps the effective throttle opening delta after the trigger threshold is subtracted, capping the maximum allowable transient pulse width. The factory setting of 35 counts limits the active calculation range to approximately 0.70 volts above the trigger threshold.
THRMAX.overview_markdown: `THRMAX` defines the maximum allowable throttle position sensor delta voltage used to compute the throttle-based acceleration enrichment pump shot. When the accelerator is rapidly floored from idle, the throttle sensor voltage can jump by more than 3.5 volts in a fraction of a second. If this entire voltage swing were multiplied by the enrichment slope, the controller would inject a massive flood of fuel that would bog or drown the engine. `THRMAX` clamps the effective throttle opening delta after the trigger threshold is subtracted, capping the maximum allowable transient pulse width. The factory setting of 35 counts limits the active calculation range to approximately 0.70 volts above the trigger threshold.
THRMAX.tuners_guide: Lowering THRMAX limits the maximum volume of fuel that a rapid throttle depression can deliver, which is especially critical when running high-flow aftermarket fuel injectors that deliver substantially more fuel per millisecond. If aggressive off-idle throttle stomps produce a momentary rich stumble with black exhaust smoke, lowering THRMAX cures the bog. Raising THRMAX permits larger transient pump shots during violent wide-open throttle transitions, which may be required on engines with high-flow intake manifolds or dry nitrous transitions.
THRMAX.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Curing Rich Tip-in Bog**: Lowering `THRMAX` limits the maximum volume of fuel that a rapid throttle depression can deliver, which is especially critical when running high-flow aftermarket fuel injectors that deliver substantially more fuel per millisecond.
* **Eliminating Exhaust Smoke**: If aggressive off-idle throttle stomps produce a momentary rich stumble with black exhaust smoke, lowering `THRMAX` cures the bog.
* **High-Flow Manifolds**: Raising `THRMAX` permits larger transient pump shots during violent wide-open throttle transitions, which may be required on engines with high-flow intake manifolds or dry nitrous transitions.
* **Injector Rescaling Rule**: When doubling injector flow capacity, reduce `THRMAX` by roughly 25 to 40 percent alongside `POSSLP`.

POSSLP.overview: POSSLP establishes the temperature-dependent gain curve for throttle-based acceleration enrichment pump shots. When the throttle blade opens rapidly, incoming air rushes in faster than liquid fuel can atomize and travel through intake runners, causing fuel to condense on cold manifold walls. To maintain stoichiometric combustion during this transition, the engine controller calculates a transient fuel pulse by multiplying the effective throttle delta voltage by the slope from POSSLP. The table provides high gain when the engine coolant is cold, tapering down to lower values at normal operating temperatures. The factory calibration delivers approximately 13.8 milliseconds per volt at 116 degF, decreasing to 7.3 milliseconds per volt at 205 degF.

When the throttle blade opens rapidly, incoming air rushes in faster than liquid fuel can atomize and travel through intake runners, causing fuel to condense on cold manifold walls. To maintain stoichiometric combustion during this transition, the engine controller calculates a transient fuel pulse by multiplying the effective throttle delta voltage by the slope from `POSSLP`. The table provides high gain when the engine coolant is cold, tapering down to lower values at normal operating temperatures. The factory calibration delivers approximately 13.8 milliseconds per volt at 116 degF, decreasing to 7.3 milliseconds per volt at 205 degF.
POSSLP.tuners_guide: Raising table values increases the size of the throttle pump shot, curing lean tip-in stumbles, intake manifold pops, or hesitations upon sudden acceleration. Lowering table values reduces transient fuel volume, which is essential when installing larger fuel injectors. If an engine with upgraded injectors bogs or blows black smoke on throttle tip-in, scale down POSSLP across all temperature points by the ratio of stock injector flow to new injector flow.
POSSLP.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Curing Tip-in Hesitation**: Raising table values increases the size of the throttle pump shot, curing lean tip-in stumbles, intake manifold pops, or hesitations upon sudden acceleration.
* **Injector Upsizing Rescaling**: Lowering table values reduces transient fuel volume, which is essential when installing larger fuel injectors. Scale down `POSSLP` across all temperature points by the ratio of stock injector flow to new injector flow.
* **Cold Engine Compensation**: Keep cold-temperature points significantly higher than operating temperature points to compensate for poor fuel atomization in cold intake runners.
* **Coordination with AESLOP**: Balanced tip-in performance requires harmonizing `POSSLP` (immediate pedal movement) with `AESLOP` (manifold filling).

MAPTRG.overview: MAPTRG defines the minimum rate of intake manifold pressure increase required to trigger a MAP-based acceleration enrichment pump shot. As the throttle opens and manifold pressure rises from vacuum toward atmospheric pressure or positive boost, the air density in the intake plenum increases rapidly. If the instantaneous manifold pressure exceeds the rolling average manifold pressure by more than MAPTRG, the engine controller calculates an immediate transient fuel addition. The factory threshold of 13 counts corresponds to approximately 1.5 psi of sudden pressure rise, effectively screening out harmless vacuum ripples caused by camshaft overlap and normal intake valve cycling while responding promptly to real engine load spikes.
MAPTRG.overview_markdown: `MAPTRG` defines the minimum rate of intake manifold pressure increase required to trigger a MAP-based acceleration enrichment pump shot. As the throttle opens and manifold pressure rises from vacuum toward atmospheric pressure or positive boost, the air density in the intake plenum increases rapidly. If the instantaneous manifold pressure exceeds the rolling average manifold pressure by more than `MAPTRG`, the engine controller calculates an immediate transient fuel addition. The factory threshold of 13 counts corresponds to approximately 1.5 psi of sudden pressure rise, effectively screening out harmless vacuum ripples caused by camshaft overlap and normal intake valve cycling while responding promptly to real engine load spikes.
MAPTRG.tuners_guide: Lowering MAPTRG increases sensitivity to manifold pressure changes, triggering transient enrichment on smaller throttle modulations to eliminate light-throttle tip-in hesitation. However, lowering it excessively can cause manifold vacuum pulsations from aggressive high-lift camshafts to trigger unwanted fuel shots during steady cruising, degrading fuel economy. Raising MAPTRG prevents false triggers on rough-idling engines or high-overlap cams, but setting it too high causes a noticeable lean stumble when rolling into the throttle. When converting to a 3-bar MAP sensor, MAPTRG must be scaled down by a factor of 1.5 to maintain the equivalent real-world pressure threshold.
MAPTRG.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Sensitivity Adjustment**: Lowering `MAPTRG` increases sensitivity to manifold pressure changes, triggering transient enrichment on smaller throttle modulations to eliminate light-throttle tip-in hesitation.
* **Camshaft Pulsation Filtering**: Raising `MAPTRG` prevents false triggers on rough-idling engines or aggressive high-overlap camshafts where vacuum fluctuates naturally.
* **3-Bar MAP Scaling**: When converting to a 3-bar MAP sensor, scale down `MAPTRG` by roughly 33 percent (e.g. from 13 counts down to 8 or 9 counts) to preserve the stock 1.5 psi sensitivity threshold.
* **Coordination with MAPMAX**: Ensure `MAPTRG` remains well below `MAPMAX` to provide a functional linear calculation window.

MAPMAX.overview: MAPMAX sets the maximum allowable manifold pressure delta used when calculating a MAP-based acceleration enrichment pump shot. When the driver floors the accelerator from deep engine overrun, manifold pressure can transition from 20 inHg of vacuum to full atmospheric pressure or positive turbo boost in tens of milliseconds. Without a ceiling, multiplying this huge pressure swing by the enrichment slope would result in an excessive transient fuel pulse that floods the combustion chambers. MAPMAX limits the effective manifold pressure delta after the trigger threshold is subtracted. The factory setting of 51 counts caps the calculation at approximately 5.9 psi above the trigger level.

Without a ceiling, multiplying this huge pressure swing by the enrichment slope would result in an excessive transient fuel pulse that floods the combustion chambers. `MAPMAX` limits the effective manifold pressure delta after the trigger threshold is subtracted. The factory setting of 51 counts caps the calculation at approximately 5.9 psi above the trigger level.
MAPMAX.tuners_guide: Lowering MAPMAX caps the maximum transient fuel delivered during rapid manifold pressure spikes, preventing rich bogging when snapping the throttle open at low RPM. This adjustment is particularly beneficial when tuning engines with large turbochargers or oversized injectors where transient over-fueling can extinguish spark. Raising MAPMAX permits greater transient enrichment during rapid boost transitions, helping maintain stable air-fuel ratios on engines with large plenum volumes or aggressive boost response. On 3-bar MAP conversions, rescale MAPMAX downward by approximately 33 percent to preserve stock pressure limits.
MAPMAX.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Preventing Rich Tip-in Bog**: Lowering `MAPMAX` caps the maximum transient fuel delivered during rapid manifold pressure spikes, preventing rich bogging when snapping the throttle open at low RPM.
* **Injector Upsizing Protection**: Crucial when tuning engines with oversized injectors where un-clamped manifold deltas deliver far too much raw fuel.
* **3-Bar MAP Recalibration**: Scale `MAPMAX` downward by approximately 33 percent when converting to a 3-bar MAP sensor so the clamp represents the same real-world pressure delta.
* **Large Intake Plenums**: Engines with massive intercoolers and intake piping may require raising `MAPMAX` to support large air mass influx.

OCTAE.overview: OCTAE defines the artificial manifold pressure delta step injected during off-idle throttle transitions. When the driver steps on the accelerator pedal and the throttle blade opens, intake manifold pressure rises rapidly. Because physical pressure sensor filtering introduces a brief mathematical lag in the running average manifold pressure variable, the engine controller subtracts OCTAE from instantaneous manifold pressure when leaving idle. This subtraction artificially suppresses the historical average pressure baseline, creating an instantaneous positive delta pressure jump that triggers immediate transient fuel enrichment and responsive ignition advance before the physical sensor filter catches up. Factory calibrations configure OCTAE to two counts, representing approximately zero point two three psi.
OCTAE.overview_markdown: `OCTAE` defines the artificial manifold pressure delta step injected during off-idle throttle transitions. When the driver steps on the accelerator pedal and the throttle blade opens, intake manifold pressure rises rapidly. Because physical pressure sensor filtering introduces a brief mathematical lag in the running average manifold pressure variable, the engine controller subtracts `OCTAE` from instantaneous manifold pressure when leaving idle. This subtraction artificially suppresses the historical average pressure baseline, creating an instantaneous positive delta pressure jump that triggers immediate transient fuel enrichment and responsive ignition advance before the physical sensor filter catches up. Factory calibrations configure `OCTAE` to two counts, representing approximately zero point two three psi.
OCTAE.tuners_guide: Adjusting OCTAE tailors the sharpness of off-idle throttle response. Raising OCTAE forces a larger artificial pressure differential upon tip-in, prompting the fuel system to inject a heavier burst of acceleration enrichment. If an engine suffers from a momentary lean stumble or hesitation just as the throttle opens from a stop, increasing OCTAE to three or four counts can eliminate the hesitation. Conversely, on engines fitted with very large aftermarket fuel injectors, an excessive tip-in step can cause over-fueling and black smoke; lowering OCTAE toward zero or one count softens the initial transient fuel burst for smoother low-speed driving.
OCTAE.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Tip-In Hesitation Cure**: * Increasing `OCTAE` to three or four counts forces a sharper delta manifold pressure step, curing light off-idle lean stumbles.
* **Large Fuel Injector Tuning**: * On engines with oversized injectors, lowering `OCTAE` softens off-idle transient fuel delivery to prevent rich bogging.
* **Clamped Lower Floor**: * If the subtraction of `OCTAE` would reduce average pressure below minimum thresholds, `MINAMP` enforces a hard lower boundary.
* **Factory Setting**: * Set to two counts (approx 0.23 psi) in factory 2.5L calibrations.

AESLOP.overview: AESLOP defines the temperature-dependent gain curve for MAP-based acceleration enrichment pump shots. When manifold pressure rises suddenly, extra fuel must be injected immediately to compensate for manifold wall-wetting and the sudden surge in cylinder air mass. AESLOP scales the magnitude of this pump shot according to engine coolant temperature, providing generous enrichment when the engine is cold and tapering down as the engine reaches operating temperature. At 88 degF, the factory calibration delivers approximately 1.5 milliseconds of extra pulse width per psi of pressure rise, tapering down to approximately 0.47 milliseconds per psi at 205 degF.
AESLOP.overview_markdown: `AESLOP` defines the temperature-dependent gain curve for MAP-based acceleration enrichment pump shots. When manifold pressure rises suddenly, extra fuel must be injected immediately to compensate for manifold wall-wetting and the sudden surge in cylinder air mass. `AESLOP` scales the magnitude of this pump shot according to engine coolant temperature, providing generous enrichment when the engine is cold and tapering down as the engine reaches operating temperature. At 88 degF, the factory calibration delivers approximately 1.5 milliseconds of extra pulse width per psi of pressure rise, tapering down to approximately 0.47 milliseconds per psi at 205 degF.
AESLOP.tuners_guide: Increasing table values cures lean tip-in stumbles, hesitation, or intake popping that occurs specifically as manifold pressure jumps from vacuum into boost. Decreasing table values is required when installing larger injectors to prevent momentary rich bogging and exhaust smoke upon sudden acceleration. Scale down AESLOP in direct proportion to the increase in injector flow rating. When converting from a stock 2-bar MAP sensor to a 3-bar MAP sensor, reduce table values by approximately 33 percent to compensate for the altered sensor voltage scaling.
AESLOP.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Curing Lean Boost Tip-in**: Increasing table values cures lean tip-in stumbles, hesitation, or intake popping that occurs specifically as manifold pressure jumps from vacuum into boost.
* **Large Injector Rescaling**: Decreasing table values is required when installing larger injectors to prevent momentary rich bogging and exhaust smoke upon sudden acceleration. Scale down in proportion to injector flow increase.
* **3-Bar MAP Sensor Calibration**: Reduce table values by approximately 33 percent when converting to a 3-bar MAP sensor to compensate for higher pressure per analog voltage step.
* **Cold Engine Sizing**: Ensure cold points provide roughly 2 to 3 times the gain of warm points to overcome fuel puddling in cold intake runners.

LOTTHR.overview: LOTTHR specifies the coolant temperature-dependent fuel multiplier applied when the throttle closes rapidly during vehicle deceleration. When the driver lifts off the accelerator pedal at speed, manifold airflow drops immediately, leaving residual fuel film on the intake runner walls that can cause excessively rich mixtures and exhaust popping if fuel delivery is not cut back. When qualifying throttle-drop triggers are met, the engine controller looks up LOTTHR and applies it as a fractional multiplier to base pulse width. In the factory calibration for automatic-transmission calibrations, the table contains a factor of zero representing a neutral 1.00 multiplier, effectively keeping throttle-based decel lean-out disabled.
LOTTHR.overview_markdown: `LOTTHR` specifies the coolant temperature-dependent fuel multiplier applied when the throttle closes rapidly during vehicle deceleration. When the driver lifts off the accelerator pedal at speed, manifold airflow drops immediately, leaving residual fuel film on the intake runner walls that can cause excessively rich mixtures and exhaust popping if fuel delivery is not cut back. When qualifying throttle-drop triggers are met, the engine controller looks up `LOTTHR` and applies it as a fractional multiplier to base pulse width. In the factory calibration for automatic-transmission calibrations, the table contains a factor of zero representing a neutral 1.00 multiplier, effectively keeping throttle-based decel lean-out disabled.
LOTTHR.tuners_guide: Increasing table values above zero engages deceleration fuel leaning, multiplying the base fuel pulse width by less than 1.00 to reduce fuel consumption and prevent rich exhaust burble on deceleration. In manual transmission performance calibrations, enabling subtle throttle decel lean-out improves engine braking and reduces tailpipe emissions. However, setting this factor too aggressively can cause bucking, lean surging, or exhaust backfiring when getting back on the throttle after a shift. Leave at zero if using aggressive crackle-pop exhaust tunes or if low-RPM deceleration stalling occurs.
LOTTHR.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Enabling Deceleration Lean-out**: Increasing table values above zero engages deceleration fuel leaning, multiplying the base fuel pulse width by less than 1.00 to reduce fuel consumption and prevent rich exhaust burble on deceleration.
* **Manual Transmission Braking**: In manual transmission performance calibrations, enabling subtle throttle decel lean-out improves engine braking and reduces tailpipe emissions.
* **Preventing Shift Bucking**: Setting this factor too aggressively can cause bucking, lean surging, or exhaust backfiring when getting back on the throttle after a shift.
* **Exhaust Crackle Tunes**: Leave at zero if using aggressive crackle-pop exhaust tunes or if low-RPM deceleration stalling occurs.

LOTTRG.overview: LOTTRG establishes the primary trigger threshold for throttle-based deceleration lean-out. When the driver begins closing the throttle, the engine controller calculates the rate of throttle voltage decrease relative to rolling average throttle voltage. If the closing rate exceeds LOTTRG, the controller initiates progressive deceleration lean-out, incrementing the lean-out factor each loop pass. In the stock calibration, this value is set to 255 counts, ensuring that the closing throttle delta never exceeds the threshold and keeping throttle-based decel lean-out completely inactive.
LOTTRG.overview_markdown: `LOTTRG` establishes the primary trigger threshold for throttle-based deceleration lean-out. When the driver begins closing the throttle, the engine controller calculates the rate of throttle voltage decrease relative to rolling average throttle voltage. If the closing rate exceeds `LOTTRG`, the controller initiates progressive deceleration lean-out, incrementing the lean-out factor each loop pass. LOTHYS.overview: LOTHYS provides hysteresis for throttle deceleration lean-out triggers to prevent rapid toggling between normal fueling and decel lean-out. Once deceleration lean-out becomes active, the engine controller adds LOTHYS to the closing throttle delta before comparing it to the trigger thresholds. The factory calibration sets this value to zero because throttle deceleration lean-out is disabled.

Setting this value too high keeps deceleration lean-out active even as the driver attempts to roll back into the throttle, causing a momentary flat spot or hesitation.

* **Zero Setting Behavior**: Setting to zero leaves the trigger boundaries identical on both entry and exit.

DECTRG.overview: DECTRG sets the primary manifold pressure drop threshold required to initiate incremental deceleration lean-out. When the vehicle is moving and manifold pressure falls below the rolling average, the engine controller calculates the rate of pressure drop. If this drop exceeds DECTRG, the controller begins incrementing the deceleration lean-out factor by one count on each execution pass. The factory setting of 4 counts corresponds to approximately 0.46 psi of manifold pressure drop, ensuring that gentle cruising throttle adjustments do not trigger unwanted fuel cuts while responding smoothly to moderate deceleration events.
DECTRG.overview_markdown: `DECTRG` sets the primary manifold pressure drop threshold required to initiate incremental deceleration lean-out. When the vehicle is moving and manifold pressure falls below the rolling average, the engine controller calculates the rate of pressure drop. If this drop exceeds `DECTRG`, the controller begins incrementing the deceleration lean-out factor by one count on each execution pass. The factory setting of 4 counts corresponds to approximately 0.46 psi of manifold pressure drop, ensuring that gentle cruising throttle adjustments do not trigger unwanted fuel cuts while responding smoothly to moderate deceleration events.
DECTRG.tuners_guide: Lowering DECTRG makes MAP deceleration lean-out engage on smaller vacuum increases, helping lean out the mixture sooner during gradual deceleration. However, setting this value too low can cause steady-speed cruising surging if manifold vacuum fluctuates slightly. Raising DECTRG prevents false lean-out engagement on camshafts with low manifold vacuum or high pulse amplitude. When upgrading to a 3-bar MAP sensor, reduce DECTRG by approximately 33 percent to maintain the intended 0.46 psi pressure sensitivity.
DECTRG.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Deceleration Sensitivity**: Lowering `DECTRG` makes MAP deceleration lean-out engage on smaller vacuum increases, helping lean out the mixture sooner during gradual deceleration.
* **Preventing Highway Cruise Surging**: Setting this value too low can cause steady-speed cruising surging if manifold vacuum fluctuates slightly on level roads.
* **Camshaft Compatibility**: Raising `DECTRG` prevents false lean-out engagement on camshafts with low manifold vacuum or high pulse amplitude.
* **3-Bar MAP Calibration**: Scale `DECTRG` down by approximately 33 percent when converting to a 3-bar MAP sensor to preserve the stock 0.46 psi threshold.

LOTRPM.overview: LOTRPM sets the minimum engine speed threshold required for MAP-based deceleration lean-out to operate. When coasting down toward a stop, the engine controller must restore full fueling before the engine reaches idle speed to prevent rough running, RPM dipping, or stalling. If engine speed drops below LOTRPM, the controller clears the deceleration lean-out factor and resumes standard fuel delivery. The factory setting of 62 counts corresponds to approximately 1984 RPM, ensuring that fuel delivery is fully normalized well before the engine settles into its target idle range.
LOTRPM.overview_markdown: `LOTRPM` sets the minimum engine speed threshold required for MAP-based deceleration lean-out to operate. When coasting down toward a stop, the engine controller must restore full fueling before the engine reaches idle speed to prevent rough running, RPM dipping, or stalling. If engine speed drops below `LOTRPM`, the controller clears the deceleration lean-out factor and resumes standard fuel delivery. The factory setting of 62 counts corresponds to approximately 1984 RPM, ensuring that fuel delivery is fully normalized well before the engine settles into its target idle range.
LOTRPM.tuners_guide: Adjust LOTRPM based on transmission type and idle characteristics. In manual transmission setups with lightweight flywheels, raising LOTRPM to 2200 to 2400 RPM gives the engine more time to recover full fueling, eliminating RPM dipping and stalling when pushing the clutch pedal in during deceleration. In automatic transmission vehicles, LOTRPM can be lowered closer to 1600 to 1800 RPM to maximize fuel cutoff duration and fuel economy. Do not set LOTRPM below the target idle speed.

* **Preventing Clutch-in Stalling**: In manual transmission setups with lightweight flywheels, raising `LOTRPM` to 2200 to 2400 RPM gives the engine more time to recover full fueling, eliminating RPM dipping and stalling when pushing the clutch pedal in.
* **Automatic Transmission Optimization**: In automatic transmission vehicles, `LOTRPM` can be lowered closer to 1600 to 1800 RPM to maximize fuel cutoff duration and fuel economy.
* **Lower Limit Rule**: Do not set `LOTRPM` below the target idle speed, as cutting fuel during idle recovery causes stalling.
* **Camshaft Matching**: High-overlap performance camshafts with unstable low-RPM vacuum benefit from raising `LOTRPM` to prevent rough low-speed coast-down.

DCELTM.overview: DCELTM defines the duration for which closed-loop oxygen sensor feedback is inhibited following maximum deceleration lean-out. When an engine decelerates with leaned-out fuel delivery, the exhaust gas stream temporarily goes very lean. If closed-loop feedback remains active, the oxygen sensor would detect this excess oxygen and command large rich fuel trim corrections, causing the engine to surge rich upon re-opening the throttle. DCELTM freezes oxygen sensor feedback integration during and immediately following deceleration. The factory setting is 0 counts in this calibration, but performance calibrations often incorporate a hold timer.
DCELTM.overview_markdown: `DCELTM` defines the duration for which closed-loop oxygen sensor feedback is inhibited following maximum deceleration lean-out. When an engine decelerates with leaned-out fuel delivery, the exhaust gas stream temporarily goes very lean. If closed-loop feedback remains active, the oxygen sensor would detect this excess oxygen and command large rich fuel trim corrections, causing the engine to surge rich upon re-opening the throttle. `DCELTM` freezes oxygen sensor feedback integration during and immediately following deceleration. The factory setting is 0 counts in this calibration, but performance calibrations often incorporate a hold timer.
DCELTM.tuners_guide: Increase DCELTM to 10 to 30 counts representing approximately 110 to 330 milliseconds if wideband data logging shows rich overshooting or fuel trim distortion immediately after deceleration events. Inhibiting closed-loop feedback gives the exhaust system time to scavenge fresh air and return to normal stoichiometric conditions before the controller resumes adaptive learning. Setting this timer excessively high keeps the engine in open-loop mode longer than necessary, slightly reducing fuel economy.
DCELTM.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Preventing False Rich Trims**: Increase `DCELTM` to 10 to 30 counts (approximately 110 to 330 milliseconds) if wideband data logging shows rich overshooting or fuel trim distortion immediately after deceleration events.
* **Exhaust Scavenging Interval**: Inhibiting closed-loop feedback gives the exhaust system time to scavenge fresh air and return to normal stoichiometric conditions before the controller resumes adaptive learning.
* **Fuel Economy Considerations**: Setting this timer excessively high keeps the engine in open-loop mode longer than necessary, slightly reducing fuel economy.
* **Timing Resolution**: Each count provides 11 milliseconds of inhibit delay.

Takes effect following deceleration leanout, setting the lockout time before oxygen sensor closed-loop integration is allowed to resume.

POSTIG.overview: POSTIG sets the minimum idle air stepper motor step increase required to trigger automatic idle air acceleration enrichment. When the engine is idling with the throttle closed, rapid electrical or accessory load increases such as the air conditioning compressor engaging or turning the steering wheel cause the idle speed motor to open quickly to maintain target idle speed. This sudden rush of bypass air leans out the intake plenum before the throttle position sensor can react. If the commanded stepper motor opening delta meets or exceeds POSTIG, the engine controller triggers an auxiliary fuel pulse defined by POSFUL. The factory setting of 13 steps prevents minor idle trim adjustments from triggering extra fuel while responding instantly to major accessory loads.

When the engine is idling with the throttle closed, rapid electrical or accessory load increases such as the air conditioning compressor engaging or turning the steering wheel cause the idle speed motor to open quickly to maintain target idle speed. This sudden rush of bypass air leans out the intake plenum before the throttle position sensor can react. If the commanded stepper motor opening delta meets or exceeds `POSTIG`, the engine controller triggers an auxiliary fuel pulse defined by `POSFUL`. The factory setting of 13 steps prevents minor idle trim adjustments from triggering extra fuel while responding instantly to major accessory loads.
POSTIG.tuners_guide: Lowering POSTIG makes the idle transient enrichment activate on smaller idle air movements, preventing RPM dips or stumbles when shifting an automatic transmission into gear or when the electric radiator fan turns on. However, setting POSTIG too low can cause the engine to inject extra fuel during normal idle speed stabilization, leading to an erratic or hunting idle. Raising POSTIG prevents false enrichment on engines with aggressive camshafts or modified idle controllers.
POSTIG.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Preventing Idle Sag**: Lowering `POSTIG` makes the idle transient enrichment activate on smaller idle air movements, preventing RPM dips or stumbles when shifting an automatic transmission into gear or when the electric radiator fan turns on.
* **Preventing Idle Hunting**: Setting `POSTIG` too low can cause the engine to inject extra fuel during normal idle speed stabilization, leading to an erratic or hunting idle.
* **Aggressive Camshafts**: Raising `POSTIG` prevents false enrichment on engines with aggressive camshafts that cause rapid stepper hunting.
* **Companion Parameter**: Must be calibrated in direct conjunction with `POSFUL`.

POSFUL.overview: POSFUL specifies the pulse width of the auxiliary acceleration enrichment pulse injected when the idle air stepper motor opens rapidly. When accessory loads like the air conditioning compressor or power steering pump place a sudden load on the idling engine, the controller commands the idle stepper motor open, admitting extra air into the plenum. POSFUL.tuners_guide: Scale POSFUL inversely when upgrading to larger fuel injectors. For example, if upgrading to injectors that flow 50 percent more fuel, reduce POSFUL to approximately 233 microseconds so the actual volume of injected fuel remains constant. Conversely, if the engine puffs black smoke or bogs rich when shifting into gear, reduce POSFUL.
